title.value: Solving Hidden Monotone Variational Equalities with Surrogate Losses
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the top of the paper.
title.quote: SOLVING HIDDEN MONOTONE VARIATIONAL EQUALITIES WITH SURROGATE LOSSES

analysis.description: This paper introduces a surrogate-based approach to solving variational inequalities (VIs) in deep learning, particularly ones with hidden monotone structure. The paper proposes a novel α-descent condition to ensure convergence in solving VIs and extends surrogate losses to these kinds of problems. The approach guarantees convergence and supports integration with existing optimizers like ADAM, being tested in min-max optimization and reinforcement learning tasks such as minimizing projected Bellman error.

type.justification: The paper is focused on extending theoretical frameworks and proposing a new algorithmic approach, specifically the surrogate-based approach, which is backed by proofs and theoretical analysis assuring convergence.
type.quote: In this work, we propose a principled surrogate-based approach compatible with deep learning to solve VIs.

name.justification: The paper deals with solving optimization problems in Machine Learning, specifically variational inequalities which are a class of mathematical optimization problems.
name.quote: In this work, we propose a principled surrogate-based approach compatible with deep learning to solve VIs.

name.justification: The paper discusses applications in minimizing projected Bellman error, which is a problem particular to reinforcement learning.
name.quote: We demonstrate that our surrogate-based approach is effective in... minimizing projected Bellman error.

name.justification: The paper applies its proposed surrogate-based method to 'min-max optimization', highlighting this field as a specific application domain.
name.quote: Experimentally, we demonstrate our surrogate-based approach is effective in min-max optimization...

referenced_paper_title.value: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
referenced_paper_title.justification: The use of ADAM in the paper is related to an optimization algorithm developed by Kingma and Ba in 2014.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Despite the lack of global convergence guarantees in deep learning, losses can often still be minimized with an appropriately tuned first-order adaptive method such as ADAM (Kingma, 2014).
